content.summary: Research priorities and gaps in acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and post-ACS care described on page.
key_points: The role of personalized medicine in the short- and long-term treatment of ACS needs further study.
Non-traditional risk factors (e.g., cardio-obstetrics, cardio-oncology, inflammatory conditions) require further attention for residual risk.

Inflammation as a treatment target in atherosclerosis needs unraveling; use of biomarkers of inflammation (high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, interleukins 1 and 6) to guide treatment of residual risk is highlighted.
The role of lipoprotein (a) in guiding treatment and as an independent treatment target needs further study.
The added cardio-protective role of beta-blockers and of ACE inhibitors/ARBs in post-ACS patients without reduced LVEF on otherwise optimal medical therapy needs clarification.
Randomized controlled trials are needed to test whether biomarker-guided management (inflammation markers, lipoprotein(a)) improves clinical outcomes, and to evaluate mRNA- and siRNA-based therapies.
recommended_research: Patients randomized to personalized strategies vs. usual care to determine role of precision medicine in ACS.
Prospective cohorts to evaluate non-traditional risk factors and residual risk.
RCTs testing whether management based on biomarkers of inflammation improves clinical outcomes.
RCTs testing whether lipoprotein (a) measurement to guide medical management further improves clinical outcomes.
Patients randomized to beta-blocker vs no beta-blocker to evaluate treatment efficacy in ACS patients with LVEF >40%.
RCTs evaluating ACE inhibitors/ARBs vs placebo on top of standard care in ACS patients with LVEF >40%.
Randomized data needed to evaluate mRNA- and siRNA-based therapies.
